# make_iso

[← Command index](README.md)

Build an ISO image from each folder, or each zip file, in a directory.

## Synopsis

```
make_iso [options]
```

## Description

With the default `-t Folder`, every folder directly inside the input directory becomes
`<folder>.iso` in the input directory. Subfolders further down are part of their
parent's image, not images of their own.

With `-t Zip`, every `.zip` file under the input directory (searched recursively) is
extracted to a `<name>_extracted` folder beside it and that folder becomes `<name>.iso`
beside the zip. Without `-d` the `_extracted` folder is left in place.

Images are made with xorriso in mkisofs mode: ISO level 3 with Joliet names. An image
whose `.iso` already exists is skipped. The volume name is `-n`, or the folder or zip
name with `-a`, or xorriso's default when neither is given.

There is no confirmation prompt; the tool starts straight away.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory holding the folders or zip files to turn into images; must exist. |
| `-t, --disc_source_type <Folder\|Zip>` | `Folder` images each top-level folder; `Zip` images the contents of each zip file. Default: `Folder`. Allowed: `Folder`, `Zip`. |
| `-n, --volume_name <volume_name>` | Volume name written into every image; ignored when `-a` is given. |
| `-a, --auto_volume_name` | Use each folder's name, or each zip's name without its extension, as its volume name. |
| `-d, --delete_originals` | Delete the source folders, or the zips and their extracted folders, once each image is made. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Make an ISO from every folder in a directory, named after each folder

```bash
make_iso -i /path/to/folders -a
```

### Make ISOs from zip files and delete the zips and extracted folders, previewing first

```bash
make_iso -i /path/to/zips -t Zip -a -d -p -v
```

### Make ISOs with a fixed volume name

```bash
make_iso -i /path/to/folders -n GAMEDISC
```

## Notes

- With `-d`, `-t Folder` deletes each source folder once its image is made, and `-t Zip` deletes each zip after extracting it and the extracted folder once the image is made.
- xorriso (XorrISO) and, for `-t Zip`, 7-Zip must be installed as JoyBox tools.
